items.title: Tariffs are back as Anthropic sinks further below its IPO price
items.summary: The 8:30 hosts Julie Hyman and Jake Conley, joined on the couch by BD8 Capital Partners CEO and CIO Barbara Doran, tackle the top stories of the day. Including the Trump administration's sweeping new Section 301 tariffs of 20% on China and dozens of other economies, in-line PCE inflation and a third-quarter GDP revision up to 4.3% that keep a December Fed hike in play, Anthropic sliding toward $78 and well below its $83 IPO price, and whether Jensen Huang is the right leader for Nvidia in a new regulatory era.

items.title: Workday beats earnings, but subscription growth set to slow
items.summary: BD8 Capital Partners CEO Barbara Doran joins "The 8:30" hosts Julie Hyman and Jake Conley to discuss Workday (WDAY) delivering its third quarter earnings, beating Wall Street's estimates but facing doubts after it projected slowing subscription revenue growth.

items.title: Workday earnings analysis: questions answered and next catalysts
items.summary: Investing.com -- Workday Inc (WDAY) beat on the FY2027 Q3 report (Nov 24, 2026), then slid about 8.6% after hours to $163.76. By 3:09 PM EST on Nov 25 it had recovered to $182.33 (+1.73%), with a market cap of about $43.46B. The intraday low was $173.00. The stock is still down 13.05% over the past month and 14.99% YTD.

items.title: How Investors May Respond To Workday (WDAY) Slower Subscription Outlook
items.summary: Workday reported past third quarter revenue of US$2.705b and net income of US$237 million, together with guidance that points to slower subscription revenue and backlog growth than some investors anticipated.
